MDR/XDR A. baumannii Analysis with Environmental Co-Selection

This comprehensive gene-centric report analyzes 145 A. baumannii genomes with focus on carbapenem resistance, colistin resistance, biofilm formation, and environmental co-selection markers. Each gene is shown with ALL genomes that contain it for easy tracking of resistance spread.

⚠️ Critical Resistance Alert

43 carbapenemase genes detected across samples. Carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB) is a WHO Critical Priority pathogen.

⚠️ Environmental Co-Selection Alert

176 environmental resistance markers detected. These genes can co-select for antibiotic resistance in hospital environments.

Population Structure Overview

This table summarises the key typing results for each genome. Understanding the population structure helps identify dominant clones, track outbreaks, and link genotypes to phenotypes.

  • MLST (Sequence Type): Gold standard for global epidemiology. Clonal complexes indicate recent common ancestry.
  • Capsule Typing (K:O): K (capsule) and O (lipooligosaccharide) loci are critical for virulence and immune evasion. Specific K:O combinations are associated with different clonal complexes.
  • ND (Not Determined): Indicates that the typing result could not be determined from the available data.

Capsule Typing (Kaptive) Analysis

Kaptive identifies capsule (K) and lipooligosaccharide (O) loci in A. baumannii. The capsule is a major virulence determinant, protecting against phagocytosis and complement killing. Specific K types are associated with different clonal complexes and clinical outcomes. O locus (OCL) influences immune evasion and serum resistance.

Clinical significance: Certain K types (e.g., K1, K2, K3) are linked to hypervirulent strains. Monitoring capsule distribution helps track epidemic lineages.

BACMET2 Database: Biocide & Heavy Metal Resistance

These genes confer resistance to disinfectants (quaternary ammonium, chlorhexidine) and heavy metals (mercury, copper, arsenic, etc.), which can co‑select for antibiotic resistance in hospital environments. Tracking these markers helps understand persistence and resistance spread.

AI Assistant Guide

Upload this HTML or the JSON file to ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini to ask questions about A. baumannii resistance.

Example questions:

  • Which samples carry both carbapenemase (OXA-23) and colistin resistance (mcr) genes?
  • List all isolates with the K3:OC1 capsule type.
  • What are the most common biocide resistance genes (qac) in this collection?
  • Show me ST-K:O combinations associated with high-risk CRAB.
  • Which plasmids are most prevalent and which samples carry them?

The Global Burden of AMR and Our Call to Action

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) kills an estimated 1.27 million people annually. Acinetobacter baumannii is a WHO critical priority pathogen, especially carbapenem-resistant strains (CRAB). This tool aims to empower researchers and clinicians to track resistance locally and globally.

We invite you to contribute!

If you find this report useful, please star our GitHub repository and share it with your network.
